title: Session-anchored I/O split pricing + enterprise SQ acceptance pilot
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Validate a session-anchored asymmetric per-token pricing model that separates ingress (input) and egress (output) rates, with a sliding session minimum (decaying grace credits) for streaming use-cases, and confirm compatibility with enterprise contract & security questionnaire (SQ) requirements.

Background: Customers increasingly build long-lived streaming sessions and episodic chat flows where input tokens (prompts) and output tokens (model generations) have distinct cost profiles. Current symmetric per-token pricing (single blended rate) risks overcharging low-output evaluative workloads and underpricing high-generation use-cases. We propose an I/O-split rate + session-floor that: (1) charges separate per-token rates for ingress and egress; (2) applies a per-session minimum anchored at session start that decays over time/volume via grace credits; and (3) provides enterprise-friendly contract language and telemetry required for SQ sign-off (auditability, per-customer metering breakdown, retention notes).

Hypotheses:
- H1: I/O split will increase perceived fairness for customers with asymmetric workloads and reduce churn during trials by >= 10% for evaluation-heavy workloads.
- H2: Session-floor with decaying credits reduces bill shock for low-volume sessions while preserving unit economics (target revenue delta < 3% vs baseline for test cohort).
- H3: Adding explicit per-token ingress/egress breakdown to invoices + SQ artifacts will shorten enterprise procurement timelines by 15-25%.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Primary: net new ARR delta for participants after 90 days, trial-to-paid conversion, churn rate for cohorts with evaluation-heavy traffic.
- Secondary: average revenue per session, token-weighted latency/throughput cost impact, number of Enterprise SQ items flagged by Legal/Trust.
- Telemetry: per-session ingress_tokens, egress_tokens, session_duration, streaming_handshake_count, applied_grace_credit, final_session_charge.

Experiment design / cohorts:
- Cohort A (300 orgs): control (current blended per-token pricing).
- Cohort B (300 orgs): I/O-split pricing only (no session-floor).
- Cohort C (300 orgs): I/O-split + session-floor with 7-day decaying grace credit model (pilot default).
- Cohort D (50 enterprise prospects): I/O-split + session-floor + targeted contractual language + early SQ artifacts package (Legal & Security engaged).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flags and billing backfill: implement flags to toggle I/O-split and session-floor per-organization (ENG work).
2) Billing simulation and dry-run: run a 14-day dry-run where invoices show the new breakdown in a "preview" invoice (no charge).
3) Soft launch to Cohort B and C for 30 days; monitor telemetry and cost signals.
4) Invite enterprise prospects (Cohort D) with Legal/Trust involvement; collect SQ feedback and negotiate contract language.
5) Evaluate and iterate; determine permanent pricing tiers or opt-in offering.

Implementation considerations / trade-offs:
- Complexity: Splitting rates and per-session floors increases billing logic and invoice size (engineering cost + GTM documentation).
- Customer UX: Need clear invoice and Console display to avoid confusion; require a compact per-session breakdown and a "bill simulator" in Console.
- Gaming risk: Users could open many short sessions to exploit grace credits—we'll mitigate with handshake-based thresholds and per-customer rate-limits.
- Impact on unit economics: We'll run modeling using historical token distribution (eng/data will provide sampling) to ensure revenue neutrality or controlled delta.

Dependencies:
- Billing engine changes (ENG-1842), pricing UI in Console (DES-121), accounting validation and invoicing support (Finance), Legal/Trust sign-off for SQ artifacts.
- Legal to review contractual language and enterprise TOS addendums.

Security / SQ scope for Cohort D:
- Provide per-customer audited metering reports, token breakdowns, data residency statements, KMS usage notes, and logs retention windows.
- Prepare a draft SQ bundle (answers + sample invoices + telemetry schema) for early review.
- security_review_required: Yes.

Risks and mitigation:
- Revenue risk if light-output workloads migrate to cheaper external models: monitor net revenue change weekly and set guardrails.
- Procurement friction if SQ bundle is insufficient: schedule Legal/Trust office hours with reps in week 2 of Cohort D.

Deliverables:
- PRD and pricing matrix (Confluence link), billing feature flag PR, Console invoice preview UI mockups, sample enterprise SQ bundle, experiment analysis workbook (bigquery/Looker).
